title: Trump Claims 'Permanent Control' of Greenland Security in New Accord with Denmark
snippet: President Donald Trump announced a security pact with Denmark and Greenland aimed at bolstering the U.S. military presence in the Arctic and blocking foreign rivals.
content:
President Donald Trump announced Friday evening that the United States has struck a security agreement with Denmark and Greenland, giving Washington long-term oversight of the Arctic territory's defense capabilities and blocking rival superpowers from establishing a foothold in the region.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump declared that the deal grants the U.S. "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," fulfilling a long-stated foreign policy objective since his return to the White House. Under the terms highlighted by the president, foreign adversaries—specifically Russia and China—will be barred from constructing military bases, deploying troops, or making sensitive economic investments in Greenland without explicit U.S. written authorization.

Agreement Set for UN Signing

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen confirmed in joint statements that the pact is anticipated to be formally signed at the upcoming UN General Assembly. Both leaders emphasized that the arrangement strengthens transatlantic security while honoring Greenland's territorial integrity and right to self-determination.

"It is encouraging that we are about to make an agreement that will ensure and strengthen the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States, and the Western Alliance," Nielsen said Friday night, adding that the accord directly serves Greenlandic interests.

Background and Backlash

Trump’s focus on the strategic island has previously drawn sharp pushback from European allies and Greenlandic residents. Earlier this year, Trump floated the idea of buying Greenland outright and briefly threatened a 10 percent tariff on European imports after allied nations issued a joint statement affirming Greenland's sovereignty.

Despite the government-level consensus, domestic and international skepticism remains. Local demonstrations in Nuuk feature residents protesting foreign encroachment, while a Pew Research Center poll conducted in January revealed that 58 percent of Americans opposed a U.S. takeover of the island. Nevertheless, Trump signaled that Washington would move rapidly to expand its military footprint across the region.
